source.title: Maximal Initial Learning Rates in Deep ReLU Networks
source.authors: Gaurav M. Iyer; Boris Hanin; D. Rolnick

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that blocks extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures initialization sharpness against maximal initial learning rate, reports that their relationship differs from late-training patterns, and shows sensitivity to initialization and input-layer learning rate. It does not measure the training–test generalization gap itself, so this is a refinement relevant to V7 rather than a direct test of the catalog's generalization claims.
record.gate_note: The study's outcomes concern initial learning-rate thresholds, Hessian sharpness, and training stability. It does not report training and test error gaps or test generalization effects. Figure 7's validation accuracy is a performance result, but it reports only accuracy at the chosen maximal initial learning rate and does not compare training and test error or test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study tests learning-rate thresholds and optimization dynamics, not any listed generalization claim. Its Hessian eigenvalue at initialization and learning-rate stability measurements do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness versus trained-network generalization gaps. Validation accuracy in Figures 7 and 13 supplies none of the comparisons required by V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's main paraphrase is accurate: maximal initial learning rate follows empirical architecture and initialization-sharpness scaling relationships under sufficient width relative to depth and a small input-layer learning rate; the authors also prove initialization-Hessian bounds and leave the empirical exponents unexplained. Its scope statement needs qualification: the main experiments use constant-width fully connected ReLU networks, but Appendix G also presents preliminary ResNet-20 experiments with constant and scheduled learning rates.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments study initial learning-rate thresholds and initialization sharpness, rather than memorization or generalization-gap interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured initial-learning-rate and sharpness relationships vary with width/depth, input-layer learning rate, initialization scheme, and dataset. The paper reports distinct behavior for Kaiming, LeCun, and NTK initializations.

fits_no_version.finding: For sufficiently wide Kaiming-initialized fully connected ReLU networks with a smaller input-layer learning rate, maximal initial learning rate scales with depth times width. Its relationship to initial Hessian sharpness is not simply inverse; Figure 4 reports log-log slopes of 1.135 on CIFAR-10 and 1.193 on MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architecture and initialization sharpness predict maximal initial learning rates under specified training conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 5 reproduces progressive sharpening under both LeCun and Kaiming initialization, with an early sharpness drop under Kaiming initialization; Figure 6 shows a different, nonmonotonic sharpness–learning-rate relationship under NTK parametrization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization affects sharpness dynamics and its relationship to learning-rate stability.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 7 reports approximately 50% CIFAR-10 validation accuracy at the selected maximal initial learning rate, while MNIST trajectories demonstrate that reaching the selection threshold does not guarantee continued stability. Figure 13 compares constant and scheduled learning rates in preliminary ResNet-20 experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A learning rate selected for successful early training can require later scheduling to sustain performance.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research 202, 2023
record.problems: The study does not measure the claim's training–test generalization gap. Experiments focus on constant-width fully connected ReLU networks, vanilla SGD, and fixed batch size; the paper identifies batch size, regularization, data augmentation, optimizer, and other architectures as future work. Some performance results are figure-based.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the study's reported measurements do not bear on any listed version's named generalization behavior. Figure 7 reports validation performance at the maximal initial learning rate, without a training–test error comparison.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected held-out performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance in trained networks, its association with training–test gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Change the reader's tests/T5 classification to discusses/T6. A different relationship between initialization sharpness and learning-rate stability does not refine or challenge V7's distinct correlation with generalization gaps. Keeping the result rows and verdict labels empty is appropriate.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Test-error behavior when width exceeds the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization on images.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking of training–test gaps; the study measures Hessian sharpness at initialization, not the version's trained-network measure or generalization gap.
Effect of removing memorized examples on test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
